entries.originalText: Blessed be thy name, O Lord, for evermore, who hast willed this temptation and trouble to come upon me.
entries.modernizedText: Blessed be Your name, O Lord, forevermore, who have willed this temptation and trouble to come upon me.

entries.originalText: I cannot escape it, but have need to flee unto Thee, that Thou mayest succour me and turn it unto me for good.
entries.modernizedText: I cannot escape it, but need to flee to You, that You may help me and turn it to my good.

entries.originalText: Lord, now am I in tribulation, and it is not well within my heart, but I am sore vexed by the suffering which lieth upon me.
entries.modernizedText: Lord, now I am in tribulation, and it is not well within my heart, but I am sorely vexed by the suffering that lies upon me.

entries.originalText: And now, O dear Father, what shall I say?
entries.modernizedText: And now, O dear Father, what shall I say?

entries.originalText: I am taken among the snares.
entries.modernizedText: I am caught among the snares.

entries.originalText: Save me from this hour, but for this cause came I unto this hour,(1) that Thou mightest be glorified when I am deeply humbled and am delivered through Thee.
entries.modernizedText: Save me from this hour, but for this cause I came to this hour,(1) that You might be glorified when I am deeply humbled and am delivered through You.

entries.originalText: Let it be Thy pleasure to deliver me;(2) for what can I do who am poor, and without Thee whither shall I go?
entries.modernizedText: Let it be Your pleasure to deliver me;(2) for what can I do who am poor, and without You where shall I go?

entries.originalText: Help me, O Lord my God, and I will not fear how much soever I be weighed down.
entries.modernizedText: Help me, O Lord my God, and I will not fear however much I am weighed down.

entries.originalText: And now amid these things what shall I say?
entries.modernizedText: And now amid these things what shall I say?

entries.originalText: I have well deserved to be troubled and weighed down.
entries.modernizedText: I have well deserved to be troubled and weighed down.

entries.originalText: Therefore I ought to bear, would that it be with patience, until the tempest be overpast and comfort return.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore I ought to bear it, would that it be with patience, until the tempest is past and comfort returns.

entries.originalText: Yet is Thine omnipotent arm able also to take this temptation away from me, and to lessen its power that I fall not utterly under it, even as many a time past thou has helped me, O God, my merciful God.
entries.modernizedText: Yet Your omnipotent arm is able also to take this temptation away from me, and to lessen its power so that I do not fall utterly under it, even as many a time past You have helped me, O God, my merciful God.

entries.originalText: And as much as this deliverance is difficult to me, so much is it easy to Thee, O right hand of the most Highest.
entries.modernizedText: And as much as this deliverance is difficult to me, so much is it easy to You, O right hand of the Most High.
